newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO says will continue to look for French deal.
newsitem.headline: NATO says will continue to look for French deal.

text.p: NATO will respect a decision by France's new leftwing government not to return to the alliance's military wing, but will carry on working towards that goal, NATO officials said on Friday.

"That (reintegration) is a decision for France and France alone," said one senior official, adding the important point was that France was and remained a key member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).

He was commenting on reports from Paris that the new Socialist-led government of Prime Minister Lionel Jospin did not consider the conditions ripe for France to reintegrate into the military structures it quit in 1966 in a row over perceived U.S. domination of the alliance.
A French foreign ministry spokesman said, however, the final decision would be left for conservative President Jacques Chirac.

"Regarding France and NATO, the president of the Republic has taken the initiative of a rapprochement... Without prejudging the president's assessment, conditions set to pursue the process do not seem to be fulfilled," spokesman Jacques Rumelhardt said.

France had set as a condition for rejoining that the United States relinquish NATO's Naples-based southern command to a European officer. Washington, which also runs NATO's supreme command, has rejected the French condition.

NATO officials said there had been a great deal of rapprochement between France and its allies in military affairs over recent years and they expected this to continue even if the country remains formally out of the military wing.
"What is important is that the 'ad hoc' arrangements employed in recent years continue," said another senior official.
